# Introduction

This workflow checks phenotype quality and sample matching, compares numeric
traits across genotype-defined groups, and inspects phenotype-guided refinement
and variant effects. Read the [genotype workflow](haplotype.html) first for
encoding and grouping choices. Package website: <https://renscq.github.io/GeneTrackR/>.

All values below are synthetic, in arbitrary units. Designed positive and
negative controls illustrate behavior; association and phenotype-guided
refinement do not establish biological causality or independent validation.

# Read and align samples

```{r inputs}
library(GeneTrackR)

demo_dir <- system.file("extdata", package = "GeneTrackR")
gp <- read_genepred(
  file.path(demo_dir, "gtr_demo.genePredExt"),
  format = "genePredExt",
  verbose = FALSE,
  progress = FALSE
)
vcf <- read_vcf(
  file.path(demo_dir, "gtr_demo_variants.vcf"),
  mode = "memory",
  verbose = FALSE,
  progress = FALSE
)
pheno <- read_pheno(
  file.path(demo_dir, "gtr_demo_pheno.tsv"),
  verbose = FALSE,
  progress = FALSE
)
hap <- hap_gene_variant(
  vcf,
  annotation = gp,
  gene_id = "GeneA",
  genotype_mode = "string"
)
summary_pheno(pheno)
```

`read_pheno()` returns a data.table and standardizes the sample identifier to
`sample_id`; use its `sample_col` argument for another input identifier column.
Sample identifiers must be unique. Numeric and categorical traits can be
summarized and plotted with `summary_pheno()`/`plot_pheno()`. The association
functions used here require numeric traits.

```{r matching}
hap_ids <- as.character(hap$sample_haplotypes$sample_id)
pheno_ids <- as.character(pheno$sample_id)
shared <- intersect(hap_ids, pheno_ids)
data.frame(
  haplotype_samples = length(hap_ids),
  phenotype_samples = length(pheno_ids),
  shared = length(shared),
  haplotype_only = length(setdiff(hap_ids, pheno_ids)),
  phenotype_only = length(setdiff(pheno_ids, hap_ids))
)
```

Joining is by identifier, not row order. For external data, report missing
traits and identifier losses before testing. Check trait type, units, group
sizes, dependence between observations and the assumptions of the chosen test.
Do not convert missing values to zero or treat technical replicates as
independent biological samples.

# Compare haplotype groups

```{r haplotype-association}
association <- plot_hap_pheno(
  hap,
  phenotype = pheno,
  traits = "protein_content",
  min_hap_samples = 3,
  test_method = "t.test",
  p_adjust = "BH",
  p_value_type = "adjusted",
  show_points = TRUE,
  text_size = 10
)
figure_style <- ggplot2::theme(
  text = ggplot2::element_text(
    family = "Arial",
    colour = "black",
    face = "plain"
  )
)
classic_style <- ggplot2::theme_classic(base_family = "Arial") +
  figure_style +
  ggplot2::theme(axis.text = ggplot2::element_text(colour = "black"))
association$figure + classic_style
association$summary
association$pvalue
```

The four designed groups contain nine samples each. This example uses
two-sided Welch t-tests and Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment across the six
pairwise comparisons for this trait. Displayed labels use adjusted P values.
Inspect the summary and comparison tables, rather than using a significance
symbol as an effect-size estimate. For a scientific report, also provide
group sample sizes, units, effect direction and an appropriate uncertainty
estimate for the analysis design.

`flowering_time` is a designed negative control with equal group distributions;
`seed_weight` and `protein_content` contain designed group effects. Their
construction is described in the [data model](getting-started.html#demo-data).

# Compare a single variant

```{r variant-association}
single_variant <- plot_variant_pheno(
  vcf,
  phenotype = pheno,
  variant_id = "varA03",
  traits = "protein_content",
  genotype_mode = "code",
  min_group_samples = 3,
  test_method = "t.test",
  p_adjust = "BH",
  p_value_type = "adjusted",
  text_size = 10
)
single_variant$summary
single_variant$pvalue
```

Inspect genotype labels and the retained variant table before assigning REF/ALT
interpretations. A nearby associated variant can tag a correlated haplotype;
use the LD context and independent evidence before proposing a functional role.

# Phenotype-guided refinement {#refinement}

```{r refinement}
refined <- refine_haplotype(
  hap,
  phenotype = pheno,
  traits = "protein_content",
  min_hap_samples = 3,
  test_method = "t.test",
  p_adjust = "BH",
  alpha = 0.05,
  effect_threshold = 0.5
)
refined$refined_haplotypes
refined$haplotype_map
```

The existing algorithm merges phenotype-similar groups using adjusted P values
and, here, a maximum absolute mean difference of 0.5 trait units. The `alpha`
parameter is 0.05; `effect_threshold` is not a P-value cutoff. Consult
`?refine_haplotype` for the full grouping rules. Retain the original HapVariant, the refined object,
mapping tables and parameters. The same phenotype is used to guide this
refinement, so subsequent differences in that phenotype are not independent
evidence that the refined grouping generalizes.

```{r refined-plots}
refined_association <- plot_refined_hap_pheno(
  refined,
  phenotype = pheno,
  traits = "protein_content",
  min_hap_samples = 3,
  p_value_type = "adjusted",
  text_size = 10
)
refined_association$summary
plot_refined_hap_variant(
  refined,
  annotation = gp,
  min_hap_samples = 3,
  text_size = 9
) & figure_style
```

Use held-out samples or independent populations to evaluate generalization.
The refined grouping, missingness rules and phenotype-guided selection should
be disclosed when reporting association results.

# Variant-effect inspection {#variant-effects}

```{r variant-effects}
hap_code <- hap_gene_variant(
  vcf,
  annotation = gp,
  gene_id = "GeneA",
  genotype_mode = "code"
)
effects <- plot_variant_effect(
  hap_code,
  phenotype = pheno,
  traits = "protein_content",
  min_group_samples = 3,
  effect_type = "absolute",
  x_axis = "position",
  text_size = 10
)
effects$figure + classic_style
effects$effect
```

These are phenotype-associated effects under the existing genotype/grouping
rules. The absolute y-axis shows effect magnitude; colour retains the signed
effect. Inspect the returned table and group definitions when direction matters.
This procedure does not
replace transcript consequence annotation or establish a causal mutation.

# Returned results and reproducibility

Haplotype/variant phenotype functions return structured result objects with
`$figure`, `$summary` and `$pvalue`. Variant-effect results contain `$figure`
and `$effect`; refined objects retain original/refined group mappings. Save
the whole object when its tables and plotting context are needed later.

The [complete workflow](complete-workflow.html) connects these steps to signal
and annotation context. [Export and reproducibility](export-results.html)
shows table, figure, object and browser-track output.
